requirements.must: Propose a valid claim graph from supplied context before requesting review.
Obtain exact host-mediated approval for the current run configuration.
requirements.waiting: Waiting for a human to approve the run's configuration in the host's dialog.

requirements.must: Record investigation only after routing and current approval.

audit_obligation.must: Obtain a current independent audit of every approved gating claim.

confirmation.must: Get the human's answers to the research and decisions that wait on them.

passes.must: Make progress within the run's pass ceiling, or stop honestly.

terminal.must: Get the human's consent to end the run.

route.description: Record the chosen reasoning route before investigation; graph declaration may occur first.

example.reason: Primary empirical route for the supplied goal.

graph.description: Propose claims and unknowns from supplied context. No repository investigation or evidence is required.

claims.text: The supplied goal can be achieved safely.
The chosen approach fits the existing architecture.

configure_run.description: After a graph exists, propose a task-sized configuration (all three ceilings plus a nonblank rationale) and request host-mediated approval before investigation in both control modes. It never self-approves or changes effective budgets before consent.

example.rationale: Five gating claims, two needing experiments; one audit plus one retry.

investigate.description: Record the first investigation witness only after route and exact current host approval.

empirica_read.title: Read Empirica state
empirica_read.description: Read Empirica state. GetRun and RestoreRun return a deterministic plain-text author view; act on its reasons, obligations, and rendered next calls rather than parsing JSON. GetArgument and GetContract retain their detailed auditor/contract sections. Inspect state after an uncertain configure_run outcome. Do not blindly reopen host UI.

empirica_observe.title: Record an Empirica author action
empirica_observe.description: Submit exactly one public author action. The result is a deterministic plain-text author view; follow its rendered reasons and next calls rather than parsing JSON. Normal bootstrap is route, graph, configure_run, then investigate after approval. Graph may precede route and needs no prior investigation. configure_run requires a selected graph and requests host mediation without self-approval. Host-owned lifecycle facts are not author actions.

report_convergence.title: Request an Empirica decision
report_convergence.description: Request guarded convergence or an honest residual stop. The deterministic plain-text result renders current recovery calls; follow it rather than parsing JSON. Current obligations and audit gates remain authoritative. Human waiting is neither investigation nor convergence.

graph.record.description: Propose a minimal valid claim graph from supplied context; no repository investigation or evidence is required.

run.inspect.description: Inspect the current run residuals and state.

route.record.description: Record a routing commitment before investigation.

investigation.record.description: Record the first investigation witness after routing.

research.record.description: Record one externally observed research citation bound to a claim.

spike.run.description: Request one bounded offline deterministic spike only when RunView.spike_backend is qualified. Design the command comfortably below the 120-second workload hard limit; the 210-second backend bound and Pi 300-second and Claude MCP 360-second outer margins are not workload budgets. When spikes are unavailable, do not submit an unchanged request: continue non-spike research or graph refinement, or stop with an honest residual.

spike.regate.description: Re-gate one stale spike with a bounded offline deterministic command only when RunView.spike_backend is qualified. A closed unavailable result admits no spike evidence; narrow or redesign the probe, continue research, or arrange operator requalification for a future new run instead of blind retries or a host fallback.

budget.raise.description: Propose a sized ceiling change through configure_run; only renewed host approval can apply it, never auto (auto projections drop this recovery).

rationale.description: Nonblank author sizing rationale bound by the proposal digest.

child.wait.description: Await a pending audit child; the host settles it through the trusted child_event lifecycle (Claude SubagentStop, Pi foreground tool result), not a callable wait.

child.retry.description: Retry a failed or rejected child.

residual.accept.description: Accept the current residual and stop or continue with it recorded.

host.repair_context.description: Host must refresh the observed governance context through the trusted governance_context ingress (Pi refreshGovernance, Claude _governance_context); do not retry configure_run blindly.

governance.propose.description: Issue a task-sized configure_run (all three ceilings plus a nonblank rationale) and request a host-mediated configuration decision; cannot self-approve.

rationale.description: Nonblank author sizing rationale bound by the proposal digest.

human.confirm_evidence.description: Show the human the pending research records and needs-decision claims in one batch: record one presentation, then submit one receipt of per-item decisions. Offered only when the run has a human ingress.

convergence.report.description: Report convergence with the default intent. The host first looks for a human it can ask; when there is one it shows them the pending research records and decisions in one dialog, and when there is none the response says so.

run.no_active.message: No active run for this selector; start a fresh run.

run.goal_required.message: A non-empty goal is required; supply the goal explicitly. No run was created.

run.corrupt.message: Run state is corrupt; start a fresh run.

graph.missing.message: No selected argument graph. Propose one from supplied context before configure_run; investigation and evidence are not prerequisites.

graph.invalid.message: Argument graph is malformed or unsupported.

graph.root_not_gating.message: The root claim must be gating: it is the goal-level assurance claim, and a run whose root is non-gating can never converge. Record the graph again with a gating root; scope you want to defer belongs in non-gating claims below it.

investigation.required.message: Record the first investigation witness before evidence or child execution.

route.late.message: Route observed after investigation is a permanent violation.

claim.research_missing.ended_message: No research was recorded for claim {claim_id} before the run stopped.

claim.research_unbound.message: Research for claim {claim_id} is not bound to the current claim digest.
claim.research_unbound.ended_message: Research for claim {claim_id} did not match the claim as it was finally worded.

claim.spike_missing.message: Run a deterministic spike for claim {claim_id}.
claim.spike_missing.ended_message: No spike was run for claim {claim_id} before the run stopped.

claim.spike_prerequisite_missing.message: Spike has no active supporting research prerequisite.
claim.spike_prerequisite_missing.ended_message: The spike had no supporting research behind it when the run stopped.

claim.spike_stale.ended_message: The spike's files changed after it ran, and it was not run again.

claim.refuted.message: Refuted by active evidence; claim {claim_id} still blocks this scope.
claim.refuted.ended_message: Active evidence refuted claim {claim_id}; it still blocked this scope when the run stopped.

evidence.conflict.message: Simultaneous supporting and refuting research fails closed; resolve or stop with residual.
evidence.conflict.ended_message: Supporting and refuting research conflicted when the run stopped.

budget.exhausted.ended_message: {resource} budget was exhausted when the run stopped.

audit.required.message: Audit is owed; spawn an independent auditor.
audit.required.ended_message: No audit had been done when the run stopped.

audit.pending.ended_message: An audit was still pending when the run stopped.

audit.unreadable.ended_message: The audit output was unreadable when the run stopped.

audit.failed.message: Audit failed or its coverage went stale; address any findings listed under Audit, then retry.
audit.failed.ended_message: The latest audit failed, or no longer covered the argument, when the run stopped.

audit.stale.message: Audit coverage is stale for {scope}; re-audit.
audit.stale.ended_message: The audit no longer covered {scope} when the run stopped.

audit.same_model.message: Auditor is the same model as covered evidence; spawn a distinct auditor or accept the residual.
audit.same_model.ended_message: The auditor was the same model as the covered evidence when the run stopped.

audit.auditor_excluded.message: The auditor would run on a model that made this evidence ({models}). Set another: an override, or enabledModels on Pi.
audit.auditor_excluded.ended_message: No auditor on another model could be set when the run stopped.

audit.independence_unverified.message: Audit independence is unverified; spawn a distinct auditor or accept the residual.
audit.independence_unverified.ended_message: The audit's independence was unverified when the run stopped.

child.terminal.ended_message: A child ended in state {state} and was not retried before the run stopped.

host.async_unsupported.message: Host does not support async children; accept residual or run foreground.

host.audit_output_unobservable.message: Host cannot observe audit output; accept residual.

host.subagents_missing.message: No external pi-subagents `subagent` tool is active, so no independent audit can launch. Install one supported pi-subagents runtime and restart the host, or accept the residual.

host.subagents_tool_inactive.message: The pi-subagents `subagent` tool is registered but not active, so no independent audit can launch. Call `subagents_enable` and retry, or set pi-subagents `toolActivation: eager` and reload the host; a restart alone does not change this. Or accept the residual.

host.subagents_owner_unverified.message: The active pi-subagents owner, package, or version cannot be verified (or this is a pi-subagents child process). Do not retry blindly: restart the host with one supported pi-subagents runtime, or accept the residual.

host.subagents_duplicate_owner.message: More than one extension registers the `subagent` tool, so the audit runtime is ambiguous. Remove the duplicate, restart the host, and start a fresh run, or accept the residual.

host.subagents_version_unsupported.message: The active pi-subagents runtime is outside the supported range, or its tool schema or launch preflight cannot carry the Empirica audit launch. Install a version inside the supported range and restart the host, or accept the residual.

host.subagents_tools_not_read_only.message: The preflight reports a tool Empirica does not allow the auditor (the refusal names the tools), so the audit cannot be read-only. Remove the extra tool from the auditor's configuration or update pi-subagents, restart the host, and start a fresh run, or accept the residual.

host.subagents_launch_unsupported.message: During an Empirica run, `subagent` accepts exactly one launch form (for example `agent` or `workflow`) or a read-only action that the runtime's reviewed versions know (`list`, `status`, `models`, ...); control, mutation, unknown-action, and ambiguous calls are refused. Retry with a supported call, or accept the residual.

host.version_unsupported.message: The active Pi is {version}, outside the range Empirica supports ({range}), or its version could not be read, so no run starts. Install a Pi inside the range and restart the host, or accept the residual.

freeze.deferred.ended_message: Claims deferred by the frozen scope were left unresolved.

governance.auto_invocation_required.message: Auto mode requires an interactive invocation or EMPIRICA_AUTO_DELEGATION=1 set by the operator. Run interactively or set that delegation and start fresh.

governance.approval_required.message: Issue a task-sized configure_run with all three ceilings and a nonblank rationale, then request host approval. The StartRun placeholder is unapprovable; no investigation is authorized.

governance.revision_required.message: Run configuration changed. Request new host approval before continuing, or stop honestly.

governance.approval_unavailable.message: Host approval UI unavailable/cancelled. Keep pending; use supported UI or start an explicitly auto fresh run.

governance.auto_ceiling.message: Auto cannot increase operational ceilings, including audit retries. The bound in the parameters says which text applies; the core chooses it from whether the run was already approved.

case_messages.approved: Auto cannot raise the approved ceilings; lower or keep them, or start a fresh run with a larger approved size.
case_messages.envelope: A delegated proposal cannot exceed the 8/1/2 policy envelope (or the narrower limit the operator set): reduce scope, or use an approval-capable host interactively.

governance.budget_contradictory.message: StartRun budgets or operator limits exceed the fixed 8/1/2 delegated-auto ceiling policy, or a StartRun budget widens an operator limit. Correct the offending source and start a fresh run.

governance.revision_exhausted.message: Auto material-revision allowance (eight before and eight after the first approval) is exhausted. Start a new run with a larger approved size, or use deliberative mode.

governance.budget_invalid.message: Proposed ceiling is below consumed usage. Correct the proposal; counters cannot be reset.

governance.stale_proposal.message: Decision is bound to a different run/revision/digest. Inspect current proposal and request a new decision.

governance.receipt_replay.message: Conflicting or superseded decision replay rejected. Inspect current proposal; no authority was changed.

governance.interaction_limit.message: The durable proposal (3) or total (128) interaction limit is exhausted. Stop honestly or start a fresh run.

governance.decision_conflict.message: The submitted control and fields conflict. Nothing was approved; use one explicit decision path.

governance.terminal_stop_pending.message: A deliberative run does not end without converging until a human agrees to the status in the parameters. Nothing was granted and the run stays active. The case in the parameters says which text applies; the core chooses it from the route, the reason a dialog cannot be shown, and whether the human already declined this end.

case_messages.ask: Ending the run as {status} needs a human's agreement, and nobody has been asked yet. Stop again (report_convergence intent=stop) and the human is asked whether to end the run.
case_messages.declined: You declined ending the run as {status}. Tell the agent to stop again to be asked, or keep working.
case_messages.unobserved: Ending the run as {status} needs a human's agreement, and this host has not yet looked for a dialog. Stop again (report_convergence intent=stop): the host looks, and asks if one can be shown.
case_messages.unavailable: Ending the run as {status} needs a human's agreement, and this host cannot show a dialog, so the run stays active and only a host that can show a dialog can end it; keep working.
case_messages.interaction_limit: This run can no longer ask you: its human interactions are spent, so it cannot be ended as {status} without converging. It can still end by converging; keep working toward that.
case_messages.host_failed: Ending the run as {status} needs a human's agreement, and the host could not ask (it could not record its dialog or could not show the question), so nobody was asked and the run stays active. Stop again to try again.

audit.producers_mixed.message: Covered evidence has mixed producers; re-run the latest spike under the research producer or accept the residual.
audit.producers_mixed.ended_message: The covered evidence had mixed producers when the run stopped.

research.citation_unverified.message: Research refused ({problem}). A workspace source must be cited as one file, `path` or `path:N-M`, quoted exactly, joining excerpts with …; a code, docs or web source must be a workspace path, an http(s) URL or an absolute path outside the workspace (an absolute path inside it is refused: cite the repository-relative path); a runtime observation that is none of these must say why no spike can establish it (payload.spike_unavailable).

evidence.confirmation_required.message: Waiting for a human to confirm research or answer a decision.

case_messages.again: Research or a decision was shown to the human and left open (Later, cancel or timeout). An explicit report_convergence asks the human again; each asking spends one of the run's human interactions.

evidence.confirmation_required.ended_message: Unanswered when this run stopped: research or a decision needed a human.

core.title: Core concepts
core.summary: The seven author-facing concepts and the single authority for argument state.

clauses.text: An Empirica run advances seven concepts: goal, outstanding obligation, valid next action, trusted observation, residual/handoff, terminal distinction, and the author, deterministic harness, auditor, human, and host-adapter roles.
Argument state is derived from the complete active evidence set on every read; there is no per-request or persisted composite verdict.
The public contract is inert structured data, not an interpreted policy or rules engine.

roles.title: Role authority
roles.summary: What each role may and must not do.

clauses.text: The author proposes graphs and claims, fetches research, requests spikes, responds to obligations, and may stop with a residual; the author must not create convergence-relevant attribution, approve its own evidence, or audit its own convergence.
The deterministic harness executes a declared command and reports exit code and file bindings; it must not decide claim meaning or convergence.
The auditor re-reads cited evidence and argument and returns pass/fail findings; it must not approve machine evidence or alter the graph.
The human resolves judgment, budget, and product decisions and accepts residuals; the human must not be silently simulated by an agent.

run/lifecycle.title: Run lifecycle
run/lifecycle.summary: Run statuses, terminality, and corrupt state refusal.

clauses.text: A run is active, converged, stopped_residual, stopped_frozen, or stopped_budget; every status except active is terminal.
A terminal run never changes status and never produces a later convergence result, though append-only diagnostic facts may be admitted where explicitly allowed.
Any persisted aggregate that is not exactly valid empirica/v2 state and history returns run.corrupt with run.start_fresh; rejected data contributes no fields, defaults, terminal inference, or repair.

claims/graph.title: Argument graph
claims/graph.summary: Graph shape and missing or invalid graph handling.

clauses.text: The argument is a strict root-connected claim-dependency DAG containing exact claim identity, text, gating, and kind fields; it never contains trusted claim state.

SupportedBy is the only edge type and is directed from a claim to its required supporting claim; endpoints are known and distinct, edges are unique, the relation is acyclic, and every claim is reachable from the declared root.

A scoped claim is approved only when its own approval requirements and every direct supporting child in the effective scope are approved; effective scope is the current gating IDs before freeze and the immutable frozen IDs after freeze.

An open, blocked, or discarded scoped support prevents an otherwise approvable parent from approval but never overwrites the parent's own blocked or discarded state and never propagates refutation upward; the public blocking reason identifies the unresolved supporting claim.

Dependency traversal stops below a discarded claim for that path only; a shared descendant remains adjudicative through every other live path, and committed IDs are never recomputed from filtered or pruned reachability.

A current run with no selected graph yields graph.missing with graph.record before configure_run mutation or private presentation reservation. A graph proposes the goal's claims and unknowns from supplied context; it requires no investigation or evidence, and may be recorded before route.

An invalid candidate graph, including a graph that conflicts with frozen semantic identity, yields graph.invalid before artifact creation or selected-state replacement; a selected persisted graph artifact that is missing, malformed, structurally invalid, or inconsistent with frozen semantic identity makes the aggregate run.corrupt.

claims/residuals.title: Claim residuals
claims/residuals.summary: Human and data holds surfaced as residuals.

clauses.text: A declared human or data hold that is valid and surfaced is a residual; a needs-decision claim waiting on a human is part of the one human batch (evidence.confirmation_required).
A needs-decision claim cannot be agent-approved and becomes a human residual.

Every claim obligation carries the claim text as required, a summary of active evidence as observed, the shared gate blocker code, target, and parameters as missing (or null when satisfied), and that reason's registry actions as next. Terminal stopped_residual views report every scoped blocked claim in graph order from the same derivation.
Active refuting research or an active failing spike discards the claim with claim.refuted.
Simultaneous active supporting and refuting research fails closed as evidence.conflict; it does not select either research result, and the author must resolve or stop with residual.
A research leaf is content-addressed and binds claim_id, claim_digest, source kind, locator, verbatim citation, result, and observed content digest where available.
Model recall is not evidence; the source must be fetched, read, or observed during the run.
An ordinary claim with no active supporting research yields claim.research_missing with research.record.

A research record is verified by its class, derived from source_ref: verbatim (a workspace path, checked by the service at submission), retrievable (an http(s) URL or an absolute path, retrieved by the audit when the host's auditor is observed to cover its kind, otherwise confirmed by a human), or observed (a runtime record that is neither, confirmed by a human and carrying payload.spike_unavailable).

A pending confirmation is part of its claim's obligation from the response that records the research. A claim whose only support waits on a human is not approved, and a run with pending human confirmations cannot report convergence. The host records a presentation of the pending set (it spends one human interaction); the human answers in one receipt that names it, one decision per item; an item left out stays pending, and nothing asks again by itself, but the next explicit report may show it again until the run's human interactions are spent. A host with no human ingress leaves the requirement open as unavailable.

evidence/spike.title: Spike evidence
evidence/spike.summary: Bounded offline deterministic spikes, their immutable run backend, and the sealed request.

clauses.text: RunView.spike_backend is selected once at StartRun and is either spikes_unavailable or an exact qualified docker-rust-v1 binding with qualification-record and execution-binding digests. Qualified means bound, not currently healthy. GetArgument carries the same binding so an auditor can interpret admitted spike evidence. No current pointer, local path, socket, diagnostic, fallback, or repair instruction is public.

Before requesting a spike, design a bounded, offline, deterministic, small probe and name every repo-relative file it reads. The command workload hard limit is 120 seconds; split longer experiments. The backend's 210-second whole-operation bound reserves create, inspect, cleanup, absence proof, and postflight time. Pi's 300-second and Claude MCP's 360-second deadlines are outer transport margins, never usable workload runtime.

The exact Docker profile permits no network, download, or install and grants one CPU, 512 MiB memory with no swap, 128 PIDs, 256 open files, at most 256 captured staging files totalling 64 MiB with each file at most 64 MiB, and only private writable tmpfs. Stdout and stderr have independent 1 MiB ceilings. No daemon or background continuation survives the bounded operation.

Only an inspected normal workload exit admits PASS or FAIL; exit zero passes and another workload exit fails, including actual workload exits 124 and 125. A backend-enforced timeout, per-stream output limit, OOM, cleanup failure, identity mismatch, or authority failure is unavailable and admits no spike result evidence. Redesign or narrow after unavailable; do not treat it as FAIL, repeat blindly, or fall back to an ambient host shell.

A spike leaf is created only from a real harness execution and binds command, exit_code, gate, result digest, harness_request_id, prerequisite snapshot, and file bindings. The harness executes at most once within one application call and a result-CAS retry never reruns it; a crash after execution or a separate call may execute the same sealed request again, so probes must be safe under duplicate execution.

Before execution an immutable spike_request is appended with a server-generated harness_request_id, current claim digest, and ordered active supporting research; the author cannot append a spike leaf directly.
exit_code is the sole machine approval authority; gate is derived from exit_code and is never caller-selected.
A needs-experiment claim with no active passing spike yields claim.spike_missing with spike.run.
Research-before-experiment is proved by the trusted pre-execution spike_request, not timestamps or append inference.
A spike without an active named supporting research prerequisite yields claim.spike_prerequisite_missing with research.record and spike.run.

evidence/freshness.title: Evidence freshness
evidence/freshness.summary: Workspace observation and re-gating of stale spikes.

clauses.text: Workspace.observe is the sole current-file observation port; every state-bearing run evaluation observes all files bound by active spikes.
Any path, state, or digest mismatch yields claim.spike_stale with spike.regate and names changed paths without exposing hashes.
Re-gate runs only stale active spike heads with their current active research prerequisites and appends a superseding attestation.

Every committed transaction links to a content-addressed observation-basis event containing the exact pre-plan workspace capture over active spike heads that the snapshot evaluated against, any sealed spike-execution capture, and the contract identity, contract digest, and host profile policy inputs. A manifest observation_digest separately describes the post-plan observation used to project newly admitted spike evidence immediately; it is not the decision basis. An unchanged basis reuses the prior event digest. On a state-and-artifact no-op, a changed basis is appended only when pure evaluation reports that freshness observations affected evaluation; continue and read-only commands never append a basis event or manifest.

A persisted observation basis makes a committed decision auditable, not fully replayable. Operational state and the public contract identity/digest used by the decision are persisted, as are identity-policy versions inside applicable identity observations; implementation/derivation policy versions are not comprehensively persisted. No application clock currently contributes to a decision, so clock_inputs is persisted as empty; future decision-affecting clock values must be recorded there before use. Full replay additionally requires all state, policy implementations and versions, and clock semantics to remain reconstructible.

audit.title: Audit
audit.summary: When audit is owed and how pending, unreadable, and failed audits surface.

clauses.text: Audit is owed only after committed gating claims are otherwise terminal and approvable.

A valid audit binds one pending-audit child_id through a private adapter capability, a structured pass or fail verdict, current argument digest, and reviewed claim and evidence digests for every approved gating claim. The immutable launch dossier must still match current goal, argument, frozen/deferred scope, and approved-claim coverage; an old child cannot be rebound to a new dossier.

A host-owned audit reservation may atomically cancel a stale pending audit and reserve a fresh child within remaining audit capacity. Cancellation retains the spent charge, native identity, and immutable dossier; no refund, budget increase, or investigation borrowing occurs. Current pending, reserved, or launching audits block replacement. Exhaustion is a zero-write budget.exhausted Block. Logical cancellation does not assert that native execution stopped; late output cannot change the first terminal state.
A persisted audit dossier must validate as a complete ArgumentView. Malformed selected state is fixed-safe run.corrupt, never a stale operation eligible for repair.
An owed audit with a pending child yields audit.pending with child.wait and no respawn guidance.
Invalid or missing audit output yields audit.unreadable with child.retry.
A failed audit yields audit.failed with run.inspect and child.retry.

audit/independence.title: Audit independence
audit/independence.summary: Derived independence and the non-distinct residuals.

clauses.text: Independence is derived by the application as distinct, mixed, same_model, or unverified from trusted normalized identities, or human_owned when every reviewed claim is a human decision with no evidence behind it; it is never supplied in the verdict.

Every covered evidence producer and the verdict-producing reviewer must have a trusted host-observed canonical identity class. Covered producers must resolve to one class, and the reviewer class must differ from it. Mixed or unobservable producers, an unobservable reviewer, and same-class review always block.

children.title: Child lifecycle
children.summary: The single child record, transitions, and terminal handling.

clauses.text: A child is one operational record keyed by a server-generated child_id containing immutable investigation-or-audit resource class, purpose, state, spent and refunded fact, deadline, optional native id, first-terminal fingerprint, and private completion capability. RunView child summaries expose the immutable resource class so host lifecycle code never infers authority from purpose text.
Child states and allowed transitions are owned solely by the public contract; a host maps native evidence onto them and does not redefine a profile-specific state machine.
child_event owns the terminal fingerprint; an identical replay of it returns the exact Inert unchanged, and a conflicting terminal replay returns the exact Fault unchanged; D4 proves this behavior.
Launch rejection refunds once; any observed start permanently spends the spawn, and a terminal child yields child.terminal with child.retry and residual.accept.

budget.title: Budget
budget.summary: Independent investigation-spawn, audit-spawn, and derivation-pass budgets.

clauses.text: Investigation-child and mandatory-audit reservations use disjoint bounded accounts; neither may borrow from or refund the other. Each used counter equals the non-refunded children of its immutable resource class. Derivation passes are separate operational state and are consumed only when argument, evidence, or obligation state makes semantic progress.
Idle checks, pending-child waits, repeated equivalent Stop, and host status polling consume no pass.

An exhausted investigation-spawn, audit-spawn, or pass budget yields budget.exhausted. Deliberative runs may recover with budget.raise or residual.accept; automatic runs exclude budget.raise and recover only by residual.accept or by starting a fresh run. Exhaustion never borrows from another account.
A route must be observed before investigation; first route and first investigation are first-write-wins witnesses.

Research, spike execution, child execution, and convergence require both witnesses; missing route yields route.required, missing investigation yields investigation.required, and rejection occurs before evidence, budget, child, harness, manifest, or state writes.
A late route is a permanent reported violation with route.late and run.inspect; it is not retroactively repaired by writing another label.

freeze.title: Freeze
freeze.summary: First-write-wins committed scope and deferred residuals.

clauses.text: Freeze atomically commits the ordered gating claim IDs and a canonical semantic digest over each committed claim's exact id, text, kind, and input gating plus the sorted SupportedBy edge set whose endpoints are both committed; every later graph must preserve that identity or fail graph.invalid without writes or selection replacement.
A persisted frozen ID/digest pair must be present together and match the selected graph; missing, malformed, or inconsistent state/history is run.corrupt and cannot be repaired.
No author action may revise frozen semantic identity; changing committed meaning requires a fresh run until a trusted human-origin scope-revision protocol is explicitly supported.

Later derived claims are visible as deferred residuals with freeze.deferred and residual.accept and cannot silently enter or remove IDs from the committed scope; an edge from a frozen parent to a deferred child does not activate that child.
Any admitted graph node or edge change changes the argument binding and invalidates prior audit coverage even when immutable frozen IDs and dependency adjudication are unchanged.

terminal.title: Terminal behavior
terminal.summary: The terminal statuses and the convergence condition.

clauses.text: A refuted root claim is stopped_residual and never converged.
A committed frozen scope discharged with later claims is stopped_frozen and non-converged, though it owes scope audit.
An exhausted budget is stopped_budget and non-converged.
Convergence requires all committed claims approved and fresh and an independent audit that is current and passing.

hosts/capabilities.title: Host capabilities
hosts/capabilities.summary: Capability tiers and the unsupported-capability residuals.

clauses.text: A host profile is full_async, foreground_only, or observational for generic children and separately declares async, foreground, or unavailable audit execution; only an exact conformance-listed profile receives its declared capabilities.

Claude's managed auditor is host-owned async: one current pending audit lets the parent turn settle without terminalizing the run or suggesting respawn, and only trusted completion ingress can resume convergence. Pi forces the managed auditor to foreground execution. Generic async support is not implied by async audit execution.
A host that cannot run async children returns host.async_unsupported with residual.accept rather than silently downgrading.
A host that cannot observe trusted audit output returns host.audit_output_unobservable with residual.accept and stops honestly with residual.

trusted/ingress.title: Trusted ingress payloads
trusted/ingress.summary: Closed trusted action payloads, private capability admission, and exact sealed correlation.

clauses.text: Trusted action payloads are closed by the request schema; a trusted action never accepts an open payload, and an author action never carries a trusted envelope.

A trusted action carries a private capability reference that is application/host-held and non-public; payload validity never grants trust, and author submission with a forged or reflected reference still fails capability admission.

child_event owns the terminal fingerprint, and a complete closed-bound audit_verdict (scope, coverage, and content) is its replay identity; an identical replay of either returns the exact Inert unchanged, and a conflicting terminal or verdict replay returns the exact Fault unchanged; this section statically requires those facts and canonical clauses only and adds no persisted replay machine — real idempotent and fault replay semantics are exercised by D4 bound-SUT cases, not by independent one-request fixtures, and D4 proves this behavior.

An attribution payload carries normalized identity facts only (subject, child, provider, model, observed-by, and covered artifacts); independence is application-derived from provider/model facts and is never a payload field.

An audit_verdict is the trusted host-observed completion bound from a previously pending audit child; it atomically admits the verdict and the terminal child result, its child_id resolves to exactly one audit-purpose completed child, and its reviewed_claims cover exactly the current approved gating claims in canonical ArgumentView order — deferred claims are never included.

An evidence_leaf is a deterministic spike result; its file_bindings, exit_code, command digest, prerequisite research IDs, and result digest correlate exactly and in order to the admitted sealed spike result bindings, not only to request dependent paths.

An evidence confirmation is one private human receipt of per-item decisions, admitted only through the run's human approval ingress as content-addressed artifacts bound to the research record or claim digest; an identical replay is Inert, a conflicting, stale or already-decided item fails closed, and it enters the claim's evidence digest so an earlier audit is stale.

recovery.title: Recovery and restore
recovery.summary: Bounded restore context, late results, and orphan recovery.

clauses.text: RestoreRun is bounded context restoring contract identity, goal, active and deferred obligations, reasons, next actions, pending children, and host limitations; it is not a dump of operational counters.
A late child result never reopens a terminal run or child; after a first child terminal, no later event may admit audit output or change child, audit, budget, or convergence state.
Timeout, cancellation, and orphan are residuals with explicit recovery action.

protocol.title: Protocol identity
protocol.summary: Exact v2 identity and rejection of every other wire or persisted identity.

clauses.text: The only accepted wire and persisted-state protocol identifier is exactly empirica/v2; every other wire identity is invalid_request and every other persisted identity is run.corrupt.
Rejected persisted data is never decoded, adjudicated, or repaired and contributes no public fields. Transaction manifest version 2 and its observation-basis link are required.
There is no public nonce, reservation entity, ticket, phase enum, CAS revision arithmetic, or artifact path in the public contract.
A refused StartRun is structurally a Block without a run. Reason dispositions classify start refusal and host recovery.
Persisted JSON digests use one canonical serialization.

presentation/selector.title: Presentation selector
presentation/selector.summary: Deterministic, domain-state-free ordered section selection for progressive disclosure.

clauses.text: Selector input is exactly the operation context, the ordered emitted reason codes, and the terminal run status; it inspects no obligations, witnesses, budgets, child records, workspace observations, host capabilities, or other domain state.

For a known operation context and known reason codes, the output is the ordered, duplicate-free union of context_sections[operation_context], then each reason's registered sections in input reason order, then terminal_sections when the terminal status is a registered terminal status, first occurrence wins, with no other sections.

An unknown operation context, unknown reason code, unknown reason-linked action, unresolved section, or a nonterminal or unknown non-null terminal status returns exactly unknown_reason_sections and never partially unions known inputs.
Identical structured inputs yield identical ordered output; the selector is a pure function of its inputs and the canonical presentation_selector registry and never of runtime state.

governance.title: Governed initialization
governance.summary: Exact run-configuration authorization before any investigation.

clauses.text: StartRun defaults to deliberative. Route, graph proposals, configuration proposals, public reads, and honest stop are available pending approval. Every investigation, evidence, spike, child, audit, freeze and convergence admission requires current host-mediated configuration approval. configure_run proposes ceilings; it never changes effective accounting. No public action can approve.

Host-private decisions bind run, exact configuration proposal digest and configuration epoch. The immutable goal is displayed as read-only context. Proposed ceilings and control policy are covered; the claim graph and host decision timeout are not approvable. Configuration revisions revoke permission; graph changes do not. Freeze preserves approval and remains fresh-run-only.

Every run starts with author-sized ceilings and rationale. Deliberative and interactive-auto runs require one initial human-approved sizing episode; delegated auto instead accepts initial sizing only inside the persisted operator-narrowed 8/1/2 envelope. After the first successful approval, automatic revisions are componentwise monotone and cannot raise installed ceilings; deliberative human locked confirmation may amend them. Automatic exhaustion is restart-only rather than budget.raise. Auto is admitted only from an interactive invocation or recorded operator delegation. Reviewer configuration is host-owned, and actual host-observed reviewer distinctness from the covered evidence producer is checked at convergence.
Goal and configuration fields retain their contract bounds. Operational counters have one source; proposal ceilings are not spent counters. Presentation interactions remain bounded.

Claude uses negotiated MCP form elicitation; Pi uses hasUI/select/input/confirm. Codex deliberative approval is unavailable. Reviewer configuration is host-owned and is not part of approval. Hosts observe the actual reviewer identity; availability, authorization and independence still fail closed. Operator hooks/RPC may answer; physical human identity and same-OS-principal isolation are not claimed. input_private remains unverified until native qualification.

Supported hosts submit the chosen human control and displayed configuration through private ingress. One finite core policy resolves it: edits remain pending until exact locked confirmation; conflicting fields never become consent. Final confirmation offers Confirm or Decline, and decline retains edits pending without opening a third dialog.

StartRun requires a nonblank verbatim goal and trusted invocation provenance naming host, interactive observation, signal, and operator delegation. Auto requires interactive=true or the host profile's delegation_env (currently EMPIRICA_AUTO_DELEGATION) set to 1; unknown or non-interactive provenance without delegation fails closed before a run exists.

EMPIRICA_GOVERNANCE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS bounds one host approval wait and is displayed read-only. It is a host decision timeout, not an approvable field or a total run deadline; timeout dismisses and grants no authority.

controls.amendment_warning: Written for the original proposal; not regenerated for these human-edited values

settlement_notices.human_wait: Empirica is paused for human governance input, not converged. Investigation remains blocked; no approval was granted by this pause.
settlement_notices.evidence_wait: Empirica is paused: research evidence is waiting for your confirmation, and the run is not converged. No confirmation was granted by this pause. The agent presents it to you at the end of its next pass; if you leave it on Later or close the dialog it is shown again only when you tell the agent to report once more (each showing spends one of the run's human interactions), and otherwise the run must change or be accepted as a residual.
settlement_notices.budget_exhausted: Empirica paused: the {resource} budget is exhausted and the run is not converged. No approval was granted by this pause. Stop honestly (report_convergence intent=stop), or in deliberative mode propose a raise for human approval; in auto mode start a fresh run.
settlement_notices.evidence_report: Research evidence is waiting for your confirmation, and the run is not converged. Call report_convergence now: the human is asked inside that call, if this host can show a dialog; or end honestly with report_convergence intent=stop. No confirmation was granted by this block.
settlement_notices.paused_for_human: Empirica is paused for you, not converged: {reason} Nothing was approved or confirmed by this pause, and nobody was asked. The run stays open: tell the agent to carry out that step, or end the run.
settlement_notices.paused_for_evidence: Empirica is paused for you, not converged: research evidence is waiting for your confirmation. To continue, tell the agent to call report_convergence: you are asked in that call, if this host can show a dialog. Nothing was approved or confirmed by this pause, and nobody was asked.
settlement_notices.unattended_continue: Empirica is not converged: {reason} Auto mode does not hand the turn back to you: act on it, or end honestly with report_convergence intent=stop.

labels.waiting_terminal: decision needed to end the run as
labels.waiting_none_error: a human can be asked at the end of your next pass
labels.waiting_unavailable: no human can be asked in this session
labels.waiting_unobserved: a human is asked when you report, if this host can show a dialog
labels.waiting_already_presented: already shown; an explicit report_convergence asks again, within the interaction limit
labels.waiting_interaction_limit: the human interaction limit is reached
labels.waiting_surface_unrecorded: the host could not tell whether a human can be asked, so nobody was asked; stop honestly, or report again after a change
labels.waiting_presentation_failed: the host could not show the confirmation dialog, so nobody was asked; stop honestly, or report again after a change
labels.spike_backend_unavailable: unavailable; no spike requests (research, graph, honest stop still allowed)
labels.spike_backend_qualified: qualified docker-rust-v1 binding (not a live-health claim)
